did.abstract: This time capsule was placed in the cornerstone of the Time and Life building in Rockefeller Center during its construction in 1959. It was opened in 2023, and the contents -- documents, photographs, periodicals, books, and other memorabilia related to Time Inc. and its publications and microfilm and brochures about Rockefeller Center -- were transferred to The New York Historical for inclusion in the Time Inc. Records.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Items in the collection remain in the order in which they were grouped in the time capsule (as described in the "Description of Contents" typed document found in Box 1):

0. Description of Contents
1. Two books published by Life
2. Copies of recent issues of teach of the magazines published by Time Inc., selected by their editors and publishers
3. Recent program logs for all radio and television stations owned by Time Inc.
4. Brochure published by the Time Inc.-owned East Texas Pulp and Paper Company, "Pine, Pulp and Paper"
5. Documents describing editorial direction of Time Inc. magazines
6. Samples of great art reproduced in Life
7. Material related to production and printing of Time Inc. magazines
8. Selection of Henry R. Luce speeches related to Time Inc. journalism
9. Assorted materials on Time Inc. history and current operations
10. Materials contributed by Rockefeller Center, Inc.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p:
In June 1959, during the cornerstone-laying ceremonies for the new 48-story Time & Life Building on Sixth Avenue between 50th and 51st streets, a sealed copper time capsule was interred for 64 years. According to documentation at the time, "the metal receptable will be filled with 30 lbs. of documents, photographs and memorabilia, which include a description of the growth of Rockefeller Center and microfilm of original architectural drawings and models showing the progression of the building design. In addition, the "time deposit" box will contain editorial material from recent Time Inc. publications and various documentary items reflecting current news and the development of the publishing company since its founding in 1923."
The document continues: "In anticipation of future historical interest in the capsule's contents, and as a token of its faith in the durability of the building, Time Inc.'s Board of Directors has made special provisions for unearthing the box in the 21st century. The Board unanimously approved a resolution commending to the Board of Directors presiding 64 years hence that suitable arrangements be made for a ceremonial opening of the capsule in the year 2023, marking the 100th anniversary of Time Inc. The resolution also suggested that the Board in 2023 'may wish to insert a new capsule containing contemporary documents which would be of interest to its successor Board in the year 2123.'"

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: According to the "Cornerstone Capsule -- Description of Contents," the "materials placed in this cornerstone capsule were chosen to give a cross sectional view of the current operations of Time Incorporated, and to offer a representative sampling of documents that have served as guide lines for the company's publishing operations. No effort has been made to make the materials all-inclusive either in terms of history or of the present."
See individual folders for a complete list of contents.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: This finding aid relates to just one record group of the Time Inc. Records. For information about the other record groups and for overall information about the archives, please see the Guide to the Time Inc. Records (MS 3009).

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Two books published by Life, Picture History of World War II and Picture Cook Book, both composed almost entirely of materials first published in Life. The first was Life's first major book publication, the second its most recent. They were chosen as representative of Life's interest in the arts of war and of peace.
